builder_plan.scenario: A support or data assistant repeats work across related customer requests.
builder_plan.change: Try the paper's memory change in a replay of past tasks, with separate memory per customer.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current memory pipeline plus a no-memory control using the same agent.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task success, stale memories, retrieval misses, response latency, and all memory maintenance costs.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Semantic Context Handoff with On-Demand Evidence for Long-Horizon Agents
summary: SCH replaces full-history prompting and summarize-and-discard compression by separating a compact semantic state from separately addressable action-observation evidence that can re-enter context on demand, without extra summarization or retrieval-model calls. The cost is implementation complexity in the agent loop: maintaining evidence addressing, deciding when evidence re-enters context, and validating that recovery logic works with the reader's specific model and tools, since reported gains come from a controlled 150-task SWE-bench subset. Failure modes include the evidence-selection heuristic missing relevant early evidence on out-of-distribution tasks, reintroduced evidence inflating context and erasing token savings, and behavior regressions when the semantic state drifts from what the retained evidence supports.
rationale: Context growth is a direct cost and latency driver for any long-horizon agent the reader deploys, and SCH is an inference-side context-management scheme requiring no training, extra models, or infrastructure beyond the agent loop.
technique: Semantic context handoff with on-demand evidence

claims.statement: SCH replaces full-history prompting and summarize-and-discard compression by separating a compact semantic state from separately addressable action-observation evidence that can re-enter context on demand, without extra summarization or retrieval-model calls. The cost is implementation complexity in the agent loop: maintaining evidence addressing, deciding when evidence re-enters context, and validating that recovery logic works with the reader's specific model and tools, since reported gains come from a controlled 150-task SWE-bench subset. Failure modes include the evidence-selection heuristic missing relevant early evidence on out-of-distribution tasks, reintroduced evidence inflating context and erasing token savings, and behavior regressions when the semantic state drifts from what the retained evidence supports.

SCH achieves 86.9% Pass@1 on a 150-task SWE-bench study while using 43% fewer tokens and 41% less wall-clock time than the strongest baseline by task performance, versus 80.0% Pass@1 for history-compression without evidence recovery.
